IS: 9238 -1979 




Indian Standard 

LATERAL SPACING OF FOOT CONTROLS 
FOR PASSENGER CARS 



( Reaffirmed 2001 ) 



1. Scope — Lays down required characteristics concerning the positions and distances necessary 
to ensure sufficient lateral spacing for the operation of foot controls. 

1.1 This standard applies only to the accelerator, service brake and clutch pedals (see 2-1,2.2 
and 2.3 ) for passenger cars and derivatives. 

2. Terminology 

2.1 Accelerator Pedal — The driver-operated portion of the device whose primary function is to vary 
the engine power output. 

2.2 Service Brake Pedal — The foot-operated portion of the primary device designed to decelerate 
and stop the vehicle. 

2.3 Clutch Pedal — The foot-operated portion of the mechanism designed to engage (clutch) or 
disengage ( declutch ) the vehicle power unit from the transmission and road wheels. 

2.4 Transverse Plane— A plane perpendicular to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle. 

2.5 Longitudinal Plane — A plane parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle. 

2.6 Point A — A point on the accelerator pedal 200 mm from point B. 

2.7 Point B — The heel point as established by the vehicle manufacturer. 

2.8 Reference Plane P — A transverse plane passing through point A and perpendicular to the 
straight line connecting point A to R point ( the rearmost normal driving position ) ( see Fig. 1 ).

3. Required Characteristics 

3.1 Arrangement of Controls— As observed from the driver's position, the controls shall be in the 
following order from left to right: 

Clutch pedal, service brake pedal and accelerator pedal. 

3.2 Distance Between Two Pedals — The minimum distance shall be measured between the projec- 
tions of the two pedals on to the reference plane P (see 2.8) (see Fig. 2).

ACCELERATOR AND 
BRAKE PEDALS

OF POINT A

ENLARGED VIEW ON REFERENCE PLANE PP 



Fig. 2 

3.2.1 A minimum distance shall be prescribed between the: 

a) accelerator and service brake pedals, and 

b) service brake and clutch pedals. 

3.3 Distance Between the Clutch Pedal and the Fixed Part of the Body — The minimum distance shall 
be measured between the projection of the clutch pedal on to the reference plane P and the section 
given by this plane with the trim panel ( see Fig. 2 ). 

3.4 Minimum Lateral Space for the Actuation of One Pedal— The minimum distance shall be 
measured between the projections on to the reference plane P of the obstacles immediately on the 
right and left of the pedal. In addition to the adjacent pedals, steering column and fixed elements 
(such as transmission tunnel, wheel arches, air conditioning and ventilation systems) shall be 
considered. 



3.4.1 Minimum distance shall be prescribed for the: 

a) accelerator pedal, 

b) service brake pedal, and 

c) clutch pedal. 

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard aims at defining various foot operated controls of a road vehicle. It is expected 
to be used extensively in designing new road vehicles or for improving the existing designs. 

This standard is in entire agreement with ISO 3409-1975 ' Passenger cars— Lateral spacing of 
foot controls ', issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( ISO ).
